MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 20, 2018

A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC) of the City of Rolling Hills
Estates was called to order at 6:07 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Zuckerman, Arata, Carman, Carrese,
  Friedman, Medawar, Schmitz, Seamans, Shinn,
  Silvano, Wagreich

  Committee Members Absent:  Addleman, Bayer, Buresh, Corman, Portugal,
  Stegura

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Assistant City Manager
  Grammer, Sr. Planner Naughton, Administrative
  Assistant Corea

  Also present from Dyett & Bhatia:  Rajeev Bhatia, Meghan McNulty

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  Approval of General Plan Advisory Committee meeting minutes, July 9, 2018.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR MADE A MOTION, SECONDED BY COMMITTEE
  MEMBER CARRESE to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE GPAC MEETING OF JULY 9, 2018 AS
  PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  Linda Cummings, 45 Rollingwood Drive, expressed her concerns with what was discussed
  during the last meeting. Ms. Cummings questioned about the discussion regarding
  drawing customers to shop on the hill and whether “customers” refers to residents of the
  Peninsula or drawing customers from neighboring cities. Ms. Cummings also expressed
  concern with the discussion on additional housing developments at The Promenade. Ms.
  Cummings.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there was an economic study done many years ago,
  which addressed keeping residents spending their money here rather than going to
  Torrance (for example).

  Ms. Cummings asked about housing units which have a variance for parking than would
  normally be required. Planning Director Wahba stated that for 901 Deep Valley Drive, a
  55+ housing development, the parking is one parking space per unit and there is shared
  parking with the project at 927 Deep Valley Drive, which is next door. The variances may
  not necessarily be for the number of spaces and rather for the stall dimension size or aisle
  width.

  Bernadette Degener, 47 Rollingwood Drive, expressed her concerns with “pop-up”
  retirement residential homes around her neighborhood and stated that residents adjacent
  to these homes were not notified. Ms. Degener stated that this is a residential zone and
  having a residence with a maximum of 6 occupants makes it a business. There are many
  interruptions due to the number of times that emergency services are dispatched to these
  homes. Ms. Degener asked if the community is being alerted of these homes. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that the process is done directly by the State of California. The only
  time the City is involved is when there are upgrades done to the home.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that this is an instance where the City has lost
  local control and provided an example where she and Councilmember Zuckerman went
  to Sacramento to mitigate the cell phone tower legislation, which gave the cell phone
  companies rights over the local government. Currently, the Council is battling housing bills.

  1
GPAC Meeting Minutes
September 20, 2018
   Ms. Degener stated that inspections at these facilities are random and are rare.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ encouraged Ms. Degener to speak to the Assembly
  Member and Senator who attend City events to express these concerns.

  A discussion ensued on affordable housing and accessory dwelling units.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  PROCESS UPDATE (DYETT & BHATIA)

  - Project status

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia, noted that the project is on the stage of formulating ideas
  for the future. The goal is to continue the dialogue and ultimately get direction on land
  uses, which will be presented to the City Council and Planning Commission at the joint
  meeting.

  - Review of what we heard at GPAC Meeting #4

  B.  GENERAL PLAN CONCEPTS BRAINSTORM (DYETT & BHATIA)

  -  Review of existing land use designations and General Plan overlays
  -  Review of commercial districts

  Mr. Bhatia presented a map on the existing land uses and asked if aside from the
  commercial district, are there any other land use changes that need to be discussed.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about the commercial recreation designation and stated that
  the area referred to as the “landfill” has raised public health concerns if this land is ever
  developed and grading is required. The current general plan does not include any
  language on this. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN also had a question about Palos Verdes Drive
  East and Narbonne.

  Planning Director Wahba provided history on previous changes to the land use
  designations and stated that one of the most recent changes was due to the development
  of the Country Club. Planning Director Wahba suggested changing some of the
  commercial recreation designation areas to open space recreation.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN asked if there could be restrictions in the “open space
  recreation use” designation which would keep open spaces away from horse trails in order
  to protect the horses.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that if this is proposed, there should be language which
  would preserve the east/west connection of the horse trails.

  Planning Director Wahba provided an explanation about the process in order to make the
  change for this land designation and clarified that Palos Verdes Drive East and Narbonne
  would not change.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked if mixed-use should exist in the entire commercial district as
  it does now and suggested that the scope of mixed-use developments be limited.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there are areas where the specifics to the land uses
  need to be expanded upon due to the many changes in architectural styles.

  Meghan McNulty provided a presentation on the various overlay zones in the city.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the scenic corridor is not an overlay zone but may need
  modifications. Planning Director Wahba stated that proposals in the scenic corridor have
  additional requirements and agreed that revisions may be necessary.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN also suggested that discussion on the historical sites within the city
  should also be included in future discussions. The Committee agreed to include landmarks
  zones in the general plan.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO stated that the equestrian community has received
  tremendous response and stated that it is important to protect Kelley’s Corner and the
  Empty Saddle Club since they are important sites that define the city.

  2
GPAC Meeting Minutes
September 20, 2018
   COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that the commercial district needs to evolve.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN stated that the scenic corridor should remain in order
  to identify an architectural theme along the corridor.

  There was a consensus among committee members that there should be a visual
  connection and character to existing landform.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that the embankments and fencing along
  Hawthorne Blvd. north of Silver Spur Road should be better maintained. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that there could be more vegetation and three rail fences. COMMITTEE
  MEMBER FRIEDMAN clarified that this may be under Neighborhood Compatibility in order
  for property owners to maintain their properties.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there are properties in the city that are in the horse
  overlay but are not conducive to having horses and there may be a need to review the
  properties in the horse overlay zone and make improvements to the requirements in order
  to preserve the horse lots.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there are not formal easements under some of the
  trails and areas need to be surveyed to preserve existing trails with the dedication of new
  easements.

  A discussion ensued on the horse overlay zone and existing trails.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about holding a discussion on the landslide area at Indian
  Peak as part of the hazard overlay. Planning Director Wahba agreed that this should be
  discussed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN asked if there will be an opportunity to address light
  pollution. Planning Director Wahba stated that there will be opportunity to address this
  issue.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN commented that there are streets that do not have sidewalks and
  this should be something to be addressed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS asked about the parks development overlay.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that this is an old designation but could be applied to
  “Butcher Park” or the Nature Center corners.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WAGREICH asked if the city’s scenic corridor overlay on
  Hawthorne Blvd. which runs through Rancho Palos Verdes is the same as theirs. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that it would be good to do coordination with the two jurisdictions.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the city must meet the states requirements on
  affordable housing.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that the required numbers should be sent to the city next year.

  Mr. Bhatia provided a presentation with future discussion items on the commercial district.
  Planning Director Wahba suggested that ideas need to be included within the
  presentations topics to get feedback from the committee.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN suggested a meeting to educate the committee on what the
  requirements are for ADU’s and discussion on inclusionary zones.

  A discussion ensued on housing in the commercial district.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE stated that the city should have provide all of the
  general retail services that a city should provide. COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR
  stated that it should be done on a smaller scale rather than the big box stores.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that there needs to be recreation.

 6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the joint City Council/Planning Commission meeting
  will be cancelled. The next General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting will be scheduled
  near the end of October.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting adjourned at 8:03 PM.
